senses.gloss: m. (שְׁגַר I, 2) dragging or casting the legs, hip-disease.
units: <cite ref="Chullin 51a:9">Ḥull. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>ההיא אימרתא … האי ש׳ נקטיה</he> (Ms. M. <he>שיגדונא</he>, Ar. <he>שגד׳</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) there was a case of lambs … that dragged their hind legs (v. <cite ref="U00234"><he>שְׁגַר</he> I</cite>), said R. Yemar, that is a case (of which, when occurring with a man, we say) ‘hip-disease has seized him’ (which does not rise from a severance of the spinal cord).
<cite ref="Chullin 51a:9">Ib.</cite> <he>ש׳ שכיח חוט וכ׳</he> hip-disease is a frequent disorder, severance of the spinal cord is unusual.
<cite ref="Gittin 69b:15">Gitt. 69ᵇ</cite> <he>לש׳ וכ׳</he> as a remedy for hip-disease, let one take &c.
